summary.headline: Jindal Steel Q1FY27 consolidated adjusted EBITDA INR 2,667 crore, INR 11,937/ton, with ASP up INR 7,500/ton despite 15% sequential volume drop.
summary.overview: Q1FY27 revenue fell about 8% QoQ on a plant maintenance shutdown (BOF refractory change), with sales volume down 15% sequentially. ASP rose about INR 7,500/ton on stronger steel prices and richer mix, and value-added share rose from 61% to 66%. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,667 crore (INR 11,937/ton, up INR 1,843/ton), while PAT was INR 844 crore and finance cost rose to INR 548 crore as Q4FY26 expansion assets entered the P&L. Management guided to net debt/EBITDA below 1.5x in Q2FY27 (Q1: 1.71x) and a sequential cost recovery from the shutdown reversing, with the slurry pipeline targeted for commissioning around August.

segments.name: Flat products
segments.commentary: NSR moved about INR 7,000/ton QoQ higher per management. HRC prices were firm through the quarter, though management cited HRC down about INR 800/ton versus Q1 average in recent pricing.

segments.name: Long products
segments.commentary: NSR moved about INR 4,500/ton QoQ higher per Sandeep Modi. TMT rebar prices fell about INR 8,000 per index in recent weeks on monsoon seasonality, while rails, rounds, specialty angles and quench-and-tempered plates held prices.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume guidance of 10.5-11 million tons maintained; management expects to recover about 300,000 tons of hot metal lost in Q1.
Q2FY27 cost structure expected to improve on no shutdown, operating leverage (about INR 2,000/ton in Q1) not repeating, and coking coal up a further $12-15/ton.
Slurry pipeline (18 MTPA design) expected to commission in first half of August, subject to monsoon; about INR 700/ton iron ore cost benefit from Q2 per management.
Cost reduction campaign targeting at least INR 1,000/ton, mainly electricity, fuel, coke, oxygen and yield (98% to 98.5%).
Angul blast furnace hot metal to ramp from 11,000 t/d to 12,000 t/d in September and 13,000 t/d by December.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 1.5x in Q2FY27.
FY27 capex about INR 8,500 crore; about INR 2,000 crore spent in Q1. Ongoing capex envelope of INR 7,000-10,000 crore per year on value-added products.
capex_capacity: Cumulative expansion spend INR 37,457 crore of announced INR 47,043 crore; FY27 plan about INR 8,500 crore, about INR 2,000 crore spent in Q1.
Crude steel capacity installed 15.6 MTPA; FY27 output expected at about 11-11.5 MT, with 12.5 MT possible via blast furnace readjustment.
Angul: two blast furnaces (BF1 at 10,000 t/d rated, running about 11,000 t/d; BF2 rated 13,000 t/d), one DRI plant (5,000 t/d), EAF and BOF 1/2/3 (BOF 2 commissioned Sep-25, BOF 3 Mar-26).
Raigarh: two blast furnaces at 6,800 t/d combined (100% utilised), 10 DRI plants, three EAFs; Raigarh hot metal cited as 3.6 MT.
Slurry pipeline: 18 MTPA capacity, 60% Fe and 35-40% water; pellet plants of 6 MT existing plus 6 MT under addition, plus a 5 MT sinter plant, to absorb about 17-18 MT/year.
Plate capacity about 2 MT/year going to 2.5 MT; hot strip mill (commissioned FY24) rated 5-5.5 MT of HRC.
demand_pricing: Indian crude steel production down about 6% QoQ to 42 MT and finished steel consumption down about 7% to about 41.5 MT in Q1 on monsoon seasonality.
Management expects construction recovery from end-August after monsoon; HRC firm, TMT weak.
Imports of HRC via advance licences cited as a pressure on commodity flats; management says value-added grades are insulated.
Coking coal: $15/ton further increase expected; blend optimisation and coke imports from Indonesia cited as offsets.
Iron ore prices set largely by NMDC and OMC, which management treats as uncontrollable.
Share of high-EBITDA products targeted to rise; product EBITDA ranges from about INR 7,000 to INR 25,000/ton per management.

qa_highlights.question: What are the new management's key priorities and expansion plans at Angul?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities: utilise 15.6 MT capacity and shift mix to value-added grades; growth funded from earnings at INR 7,000-10,000 crore capex per year, with no commodity capacity additions and no new borrowing to expand.

qa_highlights.question: Current NSR movement and Q2 price outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Flats about INR 7,000/ton higher QoQ and longs about INR 4,500/ton higher QoQ; recent HRC about INR 800/ton lower and TMT about INR 8,000 lower, expected to recover post-monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 volume fall and what is the FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Shutdown was needed to replace BOF refractory after heat life of 9,000-10,000; about 300,000 tons of hot metal lost; FY27 volume guidance of 10.5-11 MT maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of QoQ cost increase of about INR 5,500/ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore about INR 500/ton, Middle East conflict impact $12-13/ton, coking coal about $23/ton, and operating leverage from the shutdown about INR 2,000/ton.

qa_highlights.question: Quantified cost savings over next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least INR 1,000/ton cost reduction; slurry pipeline about INR 700/ton; Vishal Chandak pointed to 18-20% ROCE targets to back-calculate project EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA/ton not rising with value-added share?
qa_highlights.answer: Product-wise EBITDA is not disclosed; about 50% of portfolio is high-EBITDA, with aim to convert 1.5-2 MT of low-EBITDA volume to value-added.

qa_highlights.question: Concerns about frequent senior management changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said eight new board-level faces were brought in, including CFO, CHRO and VP HR; about 1,800-2,000 upper-middle managers are stable.

risks_watch: Long product (TMT) price correction and monsoon-driven demand weakness; timing of post-monsoon recovery.
Coking coal and Middle East-related input cost pressure, with $12-15/ton further coking coal increase expected in Q2.
Slurry pipeline commissioning slippage beyond August due to monsoon or trials.
Blast furnace ramp to 12,000 t/d in September and 13,000 t/d by December; Q1 rain-related electrical grid failure cited.
Net debt/EBITDA reaching below 1.5x in Q2FY27 from 1.71x.
Rising finance and depreciation costs from newly capitalised assets.
Jharkhand MoU (2.5-2.7 MT blast furnace) conditional on iron ore block allocation; no investment committed.
Senior management turnover, with eight new senior appointments.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term value-engineering strategy and team quality, but cautious and hedged on near-term pricing, coal and monsoon-related timing. Several answers were deflected or qualified (for example, on cost savings quantification and slurry timing), and management repeatedly stressed uncontrollable input costs.
key_quotes: We are not going to burden our balance sheet with the borrowings. We do not want to take loans; we do not want to borrow the funds to expand in the commodity area.
Our first and foremost focus is that we should reach to the 100% capacity utilization.
Consolidated adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 2,667 crores. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA per ton increased by INR 1,843 per ton, taking it to INR 11,937 per ton.
we remain confident of achieving the ratio below our stated threshold of 1.5x during Q2FY27

financial_highlights.change: Per ton up INR 1,843 to INR 11,937/ton
Increase on capitalisation of major expansion assets in Q4FY26
Stronger steel prices and richer mix

adds.what: Slurry pipeline 18 MTPA (iron ore slurry, supports raw material supply)
Angul blast furnace hot metal ramp 11,000 t/d to 12,000 t/d in Sep and 13,000 t/d by Dec (debottlenecking)
Plate capacity ~2 MT/yr going to 2.5 MT

growth.why: FY27 sales volume guidance of 10.5-11 Mt held, with ~300kt hot metal recovery, Angul BF ramp to 13,000 t/d by December, slurry pipeline commissioning around August and INR 700/t iron ore benefit from Q2; delivery is partly specified but no revenue growth % given, and Q1 volume fell 15% QoQ.
